phase_name: Interactive Workflow + Publication CLI / Transport Architecture
summary: Architecture-only phase executing Phase 144H's Future Chapter Recommendation #1, reaffirmed unchanged by 144I Section 14 and 144J Section 12: defined the smallest safe invocation architecture connecting the already-implemented, already-frozen Interactive Workflow (IWC-001 v1.2) and Publication (PEC-001 v1.1) pipeline to a user-facing CLI, without adding execution capability. Independently re-derived the current-state gap via direct source inspection: grep for interactive_workflow/PublicationCoordinator/publication_handoff/PublicationReadinessPackage across src/pcae/cli.py and src/pcae/commands/*.py returns zero matches; SessionCoordinator.perform_publication remains a permanent NotImplementedError by design (IWC-001 Section 18.4/IWC-REQ-171); no concrete SessionRepository implementation exists in production code (interface-only, only test fakes exist); no storage location exists anywhere for a built-but-unpublished PublicationReadinessPackage. Evaluated four invocation models (Model A single composite command, Model B staged commands, Model C hybrid command flow, Model D transport-neutral application service) against contract text, rejecting Model A as violating PEC-REQ-011/012/092 (collapses Confirmation and Authorization into one act), Model B as over-staged relative to what PEC-REQ-034 actually requires, and Model D as premature abstraction with exactly one present caller. Selected Model C (Hybrid): a new pcae decision-session command family (thin wrapper over SessionCoordinator/WorkflowOrchestrator/PublicationHandoff, covering invocation through Confirmation and mechanical readiness-package construction) plus a publish verb added to the existing pcae governance-record family exactly as PEC-REQ-034 already names it (thin wrapper over PublicationCoordinator.authorize/.execute), kept as two structurally and temporally separate human acts. Specified CLI command architecture (command hierarchy, arguments, exit codes 0-5, JSON/text output), transport contract (request/response objects reusing existing serialization, no new schema), orchestration ownership matrix (no responsibility ambiguously shared), confirmation/authorization separation analysis, identity and authority input model (explicitly disclosing this repository has no authority-evaluation contract, only authority-capture, per CHGR-001 Section 17/CHGR-REQ-149), session and state model (two new, narrowly justified, non-authoritative filesystem stores -- a concrete SessionRepository implementation and a pending-readiness-package store -- filling interface gaps this repository had already designed but not yet filled, with explicit justification against the 'no new persistence authority' constraint), error and exit-code model, idempotency and replay model (zero new logic at the publication boundary, pure pass-through to already-verified PublicationCoordinator machinery), security assessment (CLI argument leakage, artifact substitution, forged identity, TOCTOU, confused-deputy -- all assessed against existing contract guarantees, no new secret-management subsystem proposed), dependency and boundary analysis (verified against the three existing forbidden-import boundary test files, all confirmed passing unmodified), operational observability model (distinguishing operational logs from audit evidence from canonical governance records), and an execution-distance update stating plainly that this architecture would make governed decision-making and publication usable by a human for the first time without shortening the project's remaining distance to governed engineering execution in any other respect (Permission Broker COMP-002 through COMP-010 remain unimplemented; no shell mediation; no backend invocation; no runtime enforcement). Named a bounded, dependency-ordered future phase sequence (145B contract freeze through 145I operational pilot), none authorized by this phase. See docs/PHASE_145A_INTERACTIVE_WORKFLOW_PUBLICATION_CLI_TRANSPORT_ARCHITECTURE.md.
